Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Communicate politely and professionally with customers
Situation2: The customer asks about the delivery status
Story: I glanced at the clock, my heart pounding. The living room was already filled with the laughter of my grandchildren, the smell of my daughter’s casserole wafting through the house. Today was our long-awaited family gathering, circled in red on the calendar for weeks. I promised myself I’d be present, really present, for them. But my phone buzzed insistently—another customer, another delivery. I picked up, trying to keep my voice steady and polite as the customer asked, not for the first time, about the status of their package. I could hear my youngest grandchild calling, “Grandpa, come play!” from the next room. My mind raced, torn between the expectation to be the reliable, professional delivery person and the loving grandparent my family needed. I felt the weight of both roles pressing down, each demanding my full attention, each impossible to ignore.
